body: Some issues: - The icon is not centered in the line. - The popup is not at the icon when the icon is clicked. When the shortcut is used, it is good to have at the caret, but it should be at the icon when using the mouse. - Hovering over the icon should change the mouse cursor to not be the text editing bar. - Hovering over the icon should show a tooltip saying what it does like "Show Code Actions" and the shortcut. > Multi-document undo redo (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114168#issuecomment-3830464005)

Do any of the current Code Actions work on multiple documents at once? If none of the current actions need it could be done later.
I tested how VSCode handles multiple document undo redo, and they work as long as the files are at the same undo level as when the action was done (a warning shows if any documents were changed and couldn't do the undo/redo with the rest). We don't have anything for it yet, but it makes sense to me to have it work across multiple documents for code actions.
I have a plan of how the undo/redo can work with multiple documents:
1. When a multi-document edit happens, save the file names and their undo versions (`TextEdit::get_version()`) in a new undo stack on ScriptEditor
2. Intercept undo and redo action handling before the TextEdit gets it (either with existing `_text_edit_gui_input` or a new one in ScriptEditor). On undo/redo, if the TextEdit current undo version matches the undo version in the current item in the stack, then we are going to do a multi-document undo/redo. If it does not match, don't accept the event and let TextEdit get the undo/redo like normal.
3. For the multi-document undo/redo, accept the undo/redo event, do an undo/redo in the current TextEdit, and check all the other files saved in the current undo stack item. If they are open and if their current undo version matches then undo/redo in those TextEdits too. And then move the stack position to the previous/next item.
	1. If the undo version does not match, warn the user about all the files that failed.
4. When a document is closed, go through all items in the undo stack and mark that file if it has it so it can no longer be a part of the multi-document undo/redo. This is because the TextEdit undo/redo stack is not saved when its closed.

> So, I think this would need to be addressed with a separate PR that changes the UNTYPED_DECLARATION warning to only show for the declaration line. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114168/#issuecomment-4196115803

Similar to `UNTYPED_DECLARATION`, warnings that apply to the entire class highlight the entire class over LSP, such as `redundant_static_unload` and `missing_tool`. These should also probably be limited to just the class declaration line since highlighting the entire file isn't helpful. Also for a future PR.
The script editor has a custom limit to make sure the warnings aren't too long which is why it only shows on the LSP side (`ScriptTextEditor::_update_background_color`).

---
Tested for lots of warnings in editor and over LSP, it mostly works well.

Class-level warnings caused code actions to not work at all over LSP, (like `missing_tool` and `redundant_static_unload`) it just says no code actions available. If those warnings are not present, then it works fine for other warnings.

Tested in ScriptEditor and external editor over LSP.
Editor code looks good.
